chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding a slave who slandered a free, married woman, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped eighty (lashes) because he is whipped for her rights.'

key_terms.قَذَفَ: He slandered (specifically qadhf, giving evidence or accusing of zina)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for a slave who slanders a free married woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the slave's penalty of eighty lashes is derived specifically from the woman's personal right (haqq al-mar'ah) rather than the public right, distinguishing it from the general hadd of qadhf. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the status of the slave affects the magnitude of the punishment, yet the underlying cause remains the slander against the chaste woman. It underscores the legal nuance in applying fixed punishments based on the plaintiff's status and the defendant's social rank.
